userStories.title: Failed dispatches record spent usage
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry SessionTurnError usage and role attribution through dispatch errors into durable cost-ledger rows and separate failed-spend totals.

**Motivation** — A run-op whose turn throws spends real money and writes no usage to the cost ledger.

**Approach** — `DispatchErrorEvent` — `src/runtime/dispatch-events.ts:130` (US-001)
- Baseline: `{ kind: "error"; origin; agentName; stage; storyId?; errorCode; errorMessage; prompt?; durationMs; timestamp; resolvedPermissions; callId?; scopeId? }`
- Target: the same, plus four optional fields — `sessionRole?: string`, `tokenUsage?: TokenUsage`, `estimatedCostUsd?: number`, `exactCostUsd?: number`. `TokenUsage` is the one already imported at `src/runtime/dispatch-events.ts:1` from `../agents/cost` (`src/agents/cost/types.ts:16`) — **not** the same-named interface at `src/metrics/types.ts:12`. All four are optional, so existing constructions stay valid.

**Approach** — `buildDispatchErrorEvent` — `src/agents/manager-dispatch.ts:178` (US-001)
- Baseline: input `{ origin; agentName; stage; storyId?; error: unknown; prompt?; resolvedPermissions; callId?; scopeId?; startedAt }`.
- Target: the three per-call id fields `storyId` / `callId` / `scopeId` are replaced by a single `dispatchOptions: { storyId?: string; callId?: string; scopeId?: string; sessionRole?: string }`, and the function reads `tokenUsage`, `estimatedCostUsd` and `exactCostUsd` off the thrown value when it is a `SessionTurnError`, leaving them undefined otherwise.
- Collapsing three fields into one is deliberate: both call sites live in `src/agents/manager.ts`, which is grandfathered at 786 lines in `scripts/baselines/file-sizes-baseline.json` against a 600-line limit and **may not grow**. Passing the existing `opts` / `options` object as `dispatchOptions` removes two lines at each call site.

**Approach** — `CostErrorEvent` — `src/runtime/cost-aggregator.ts:89` (US-001)
- Baseline: `{ kind: "error"; ts; runId; projectKey?; schemaVersion?; agentName; model?; stage?; storyId?; callId?; scopeId?; errorCode; durationMs }`
- Target: the same, plus `sessionRole?: string`, `tokens?: { input: number; output: number; cacheRead?: number; cacheWrite?: number }`, `estimatedCostUsd?: number`, `exactCostUsd?: number`, `costUsd?: number`. `tokens` stays **optional and is left undefined** when the dispatch error carried no usage — a zeroed `tokens` would re-create the "failed vs cost zero" ambiguity the `kind` discriminator was added for (#1433).

**Approach** — `CostSnapshot` — `src/runtime/cost-aggregator.ts:110` (US-001)
- Baseline: `{ totalCostUsd; totalEstimatedCostUsd; totalExactCostUsd; totalInputTokens; …; errorCount }`
- Target: the same, plus `totalErrorCostUsd: number` — the summed `costUsd` of error rows. `totalCostUsd` keeps its current meaning (successful spend only), so failed spend becomes visible without silently re-basing every historical comparison.

**Scope** — In: error-event construction, AgentManager call-site reshaping, error cost mapping/serialization, and aggregate error-spend totals. Out: reporting failed spend in the `nax cost` CLI output; adding model attribution (`model`, `pricingSource`) to `DispatchErrorEvent`.

**Interface**
```typescript
dispatchOptions: { storyId?: string; callId?: string; scopeId?: string; sessionRole?: string }
sessionRole?: string
tokenUsage?: TokenUsage
estimatedCostUsd?: number
exactCostUsd?: number
tokens?: { input: number; output: number; cacheRead?: number; cacheWrite?: number }
costUsd?: number
totalErrorCostUsd: number
```
acceptanceCriteria: buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose tokenUsage equals the SessionTurnError tokenUsage when given a SessionTurnError carrying tokenUsage, estimatedCostUsd, and exactCostUsd.
buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose estimatedCostUsd equals the SessionTurnError estimatedCostUsd when given that SessionTurnError.
buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose exactCostUsd equals the SessionTurnError exactCostUsd when given that SessionTurnError.
buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose tokenUsage, estimatedCostUsd, and exactCostUsd are undefined when given a plain Error.
buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose tokenUsage is undefined and whose errorCode and durationMs are populated when given a SessionTurnError whose tokenUsage is undefined.
buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose sessionRole, storyId, callId, and scopeId equal the corresponding dispatchOptions fields.
buildDispatchErrorEvent returns a DispatchErrorEvent whose sessionRole is undefined when dispatchOptions omits sessionRole.

When attachCostSubscriber receives a DispatchErrorEvent carrying tokenUsage and exactCostUsd, it records a CostErrorEvent whose tokens.input, tokens.output, estimatedCostUsd, exactCostUsd, and sessionRole match the emitted event.
When attachCostSubscriber receives a DispatchErrorEvent with no tokenUsage, it records a CostErrorEvent whose tokens is undefined rather than an object of zeros.
When attachCostSubscriber receives a dispatch error with exactCostUsd, the recorded CostErrorEvent.costUsd equals exactCostUsd.
When attachCostSubscriber receives a dispatch error carrying only estimatedCostUsd, the recorded CostErrorEvent.costUsd equals estimatedCostUsd.
CostAggregator.snapshot() returns totalErrorCostUsd equal to the summed costUsd of recorded error events, with totalCostUsd unchanged by those error events.
After CostAggregator.drain(), the written <runId>.jsonl contains an error row whose tokens and costUsd equal the recorded values alongside its errorCode.

Given sendPrompt stubbed to throw a SessionTurnError carrying tokenUsage and exactCostUsd, when AgentManager.runAsSession is called, then it emits a dispatch-error event carrying that tokenUsage and exactCostUsd and rethrows the error.

routing.reasoning: Crosses dispatch typing, manager call sites, middleware mapping, aggregation, and persisted JSONL while preserving historical total semantics.

outOfScope: US-001 only: reporting failed spend in the `nax cost` CLI output.
Adding model attribution (`model`, `pricingSource`) to `DispatchErrorEvent`; only `sessionRole` and usage are added.

userStories.title: Sweep retained transcripts at run setup
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make native transcript retention enforce its cap even when warm sessions never reach the close path.

**Motivation** — A warm-lifetime native session is never closed, so its transcript is never deleted and the retention cap structurally cannot see it.

**Approach** — `pruneRetainedTranscripts` — `src/agents/native/session/transcript-store.ts:165` (US-002)
- Baseline: `pruneRetainedTranscripts(dir: string, maxRetained = MAX_RETAINED_TRANSCRIPTS): Promise<void>`
- Target: same parameters, returns `Promise<number>` — the count of files deleted. Its one existing caller (`src/agents/native/session/session.ts:157`) ignores the return value.

**Approach** — `sweepFeatureTranscripts` — new, `src/session/transcript-sweep.ts` (US-002)
- Target: `sweepFeatureTranscripts(opts: { featureName?: string; transcriptRoot?: string; dryRun?: boolean }): Promise<number>`. Derives the directory through `deriveNativeTranscriptDir` (`src/session/manager-deps.ts:45`) — the documented SSOT for the transcript path (ADR-028 §3), imported relatively from `./manager-deps` — and delegates to `pruneRetainedTranscripts`, imported from the `@/agents/native` nested barrel. Returns `0` without touching disk when the directory cannot be derived or `dryRun` is true. Exported from the `@/session` barrel; the `@/agents/native` barrel gains a `pruneRetainedTranscripts` re-export.
- It mirrors the file shape of `src/session/scratch-purge.ts` (a feature-scoped sessions-directory sweep with injectable deps). Note that `purgeStaleScratch` has no production caller today despite its docstring — it is a shape precedent only, not evidence of an existing run-end hook.

**Approach** — `setupRun` — `src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:187` (US-002)
- Baseline: at `:381` it calls `sessionManager.sweepOrphans()` and logs the count.
- Target: the same block also calls `sweepFeatureTranscripts` with the run's `feature` and `runtime.outputDir` (`NaxRuntime.outputDir`, `src/runtime/index.ts:124`; it is the value threaded to `SessionManager` as `transcriptRoot` at `src/runtime/index.ts:304`) and `runtime.dryRun`, logging the deleted count when non-zero. Sweeping here rather than at run end is what makes the cap independent of any close.

**Scope** — In: counted pruning, a feature-scoped sweep utility and barrel exports, and startup invocation. Out: closing warm-lifetime native sessions at run end; changing `MAX_RETAINED_TRANSCRIPTS` from 50, or making it configurable; wiring `purgeStaleScratch`.

**Interface**
```typescript
pruneRetainedTranscripts(dir: string, maxRetained = MAX_RETAINED_TRANSCRIPTS): Promise<number>
sweepFeatureTranscripts(opts: { featureName?: string; transcriptRoot?: string; dryRun?: boolean }): Promise<number>
```
acceptanceCriteria: pruneRetainedTranscripts returns 3 when it deletes the excess from a directory holding 53 transcript files with maxRetained 50.
pruneRetainedTranscripts returns 0 and deletes nothing when the directory holds fewer transcript files than maxRetained.
pruneRetainedTranscripts deletes oldest transcript files by mtime first, leaving exactly the maxRetained most recently modified files.
sweepFeatureTranscripts prunes <transcriptRoot>/features/<featureName>/sessions to MAX_RETAINED_TRANSCRIPTS and returns the deleted count when given featureName and transcriptRoot.
sweepFeatureTranscripts deletes a live-name <name>.transcript.json file as readily as a failed-<stamp> file when the directory is over the cap.
sweepFeatureTranscripts returns 0 and deletes nothing when featureName is undefined.
sweepFeatureTranscripts returns 0 and deletes nothing when transcriptRoot is undefined.
sweepFeatureTranscripts returns 0 and deletes nothing when dryRun is true, even for a directory over the cap.
sweepFeatureTranscripts returns 0 when the derived directory does not exist.
Given sweepFeatureTranscripts stubbed, when setupRun runs, then it invokes the sweep exactly once with the run feature as featureName and runtime outputDir as transcriptRoot.
Given sweepFeatureTranscripts stubbed, when setupRun runs under dryRun true, then it invokes the sweep with dryRun true.

routing.reasoning: Adds a filesystem sweep and wires it into lifecycle setup; it operates on session artifacts, requiring strict session-path test isolation.

outOfScope: Closing warm-lifetime native sessions at run end; retention is made independent of the close path instead.
Changing `MAX_RETAINED_TRANSCRIPTS` from 50, or making it configurable.
Wiring `purgeStaleScratch`, which has no production caller today.

userStories.title: Preserve audited coding-tool runtime in tracked sessions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve audited coding-tool support for tracked sessions without replacing a runtime supplied by the caller.

**Motivation** — `runTrackedSession` builds coding-tool support with a no-op audit sink and overwrites the caller's recording runtime.

**Approach** — `runTrackedSession` — `src/session/manager-run.ts:70` (US-003)
- Baseline: calls `buildCodingToolSupport({ root, grants, declared, storyId })` and unconditionally spreads `codingToolRuntime` / `codingTools` into the injected `runOptions`.
- Target: calls `resolveCodingToolSupport(request.runOptions)` (`src/agents/coding-tool-support.ts:103`) — which derives `auditDir` via `toolAuditDir` and the ledger name via `buildLedgerSessionName`, and therefore records — and applies the result **only when** `request.runOptions.codingToolRuntime` is `undefined`, so a caller that already built a recording runtime keeps it.

**Scope** — In: tracked-session coding-tool support resolution and caller-runtime preservation. Out: wiring a production caller for `SessionRunClient`; `runTrackedSession` stays reachable only from `SessionManager.runInSession`.

**Interface**
```typescript
resolveCodingToolSupport(options): CodingToolSupport | undefined
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given SessionManager.runInSession with a SessionRunClient, declared coding tools, a codingToolRoot, an outputDir, and no caller-supplied codingToolRuntime, when the received runtime dispatches a tool call, then a ledger record is written under the audit directory derived by toolAuditDir from those options.
runTrackedSession passes the runner runOptions.codingTools equal to the advertised tools for the declared set when declaredTools is non-empty and no caller-supplied codingToolRuntime exists.
runTrackedSession passes the runner the same codingToolRuntime instance supplied by the caller when one is supplied.
runTrackedSession passes the runner runOptions.codingToolRuntime as undefined when declaredTools is empty and no caller-supplied runtime exists.
runTrackedSession rejects with a NaxError whose code is CODING_TOOL_ROOT_MISSING when declaredTools is non-empty and codingToolRoot is an empty string.
Given SessionManager.runInSession with a SessionRunClient and declared tools, when the runner receives the request, then runOptions.codingToolRuntime is defined and the session state is RUNNING.

routing.reasoning: Changes session-run wiring that grants tool execution capability and audit evidence, so strict isolation is appropriate.

outOfScope: Wiring a production caller for `SessionRunClient`; `runTrackedSession` stays reachable only from `SessionManager.runInSession`.

userStories.title: Claim project identity before plan dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Ensure every nax plan mode claims its project identity before it can dispatch paid plan work.

**Motivation** — `nax plan` never claims the project identity, so two checkouts sharing a project name mix their cost records in one directory.

**Approach** — `planCommand` — `src/cli/plan-command.ts:79` (US-004)
- Baseline: `planCommand(workdir, config, options)` calls `buildPlanModeContext` immediately.
- Target: the same signature; before `buildPlanModeContext`, it claims the project identity via a new `_planDeps.claimProjectIdentity` entry (`src/cli/plan-runtime.ts`), defaulting to `claimProjectIdentity` from `@/runtime`. `projectKey` is derived exactly as `run-setup.ts:350` derives it: `config.name?.trim() || basename(workdir)`. `remoteUrl` is resolved the same way, via `_planDeps.spawnSync(["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"])`, and is `null` when that fails.
- `planCommand` is the sole `nax plan` entry point — `bin/nax.ts:426` and `bin/nax.ts:1045` both route through it, and pipeline mode is reached from inside it via `createPlanStrategy`, so one claim covers every plan mode.

**Scope** — In: injected plan identity claim, project-key and origin-URL derivation, collision propagation, and warn-and-proceed handling for other failures. Out: any change to `nax migrate --reclaim` / `--merge`, or to collision recovery generally; extending the collision guard to `nax resume`, `nax replay`, or any command other than `nax plan`.

**Interface**
```typescript
claimProjectIdentity(projectKey, workdir, remoteUrl): Promise<void>
```
acceptanceCriteria: planCommand rejects with a NaxError whose code is RUN_NAME_COLLISION when the derived projectKey identity is registered to a different workdir.
When planCommand encounters a RUN_NAME_COLLISION identity claim, then the plan strategy execute method is never invoked.
When no identity exists for the derived projectKey, planCommand writes an identity whose workdir equals its workdir argument and invokes the plan strategy once.
When the derived projectKey identity is already registered to the same workdir, planCommand invokes the plan strategy once and updates the stored lastSeen.
planCommand claims under the trimmed config.name when config.name is a non-empty string.
planCommand claims under basename(workdir) when config.name is absent or only whitespace.
planCommand passes the trimmed origin remote URL as remoteUrl when _planDeps.spawnSync reports exit code 0.
planCommand passes null as remoteUrl when _planDeps.spawnSync reports a non-zero exit code.
When _planDeps.claimProjectIdentity rejects with an error whose code is not RUN_NAME_COLLISION, then planCommand invokes the plan strategy once and resolves.

routing.reasoning: A focused CLI preflight and dependency-injection change with established identity and plan-test conventions.

outOfScope: Any change to `nax migrate --reclaim` / `--merge`, or to collision recovery generally.
Extending the collision guard to `nax resume`, `nax replay`, or any command other than `nax plan`.

analysis:
This is an enhancement of existing TypeScript dispatch, accounting, session, and CLI infrastructure. US-001 changes the error-event boundary in src/agents/manager-dispatch.ts:178 and its two AgentManager call sites (src/agents/manager.ts:693,745), then maps the newly carried attribution and usage through src/runtime/middleware/cost.ts:91 into CostErrorEvent and CostSnapshot in src/runtime/cost-aggregator.ts:89-110. SessionTurnError already carries the required usage/cost values at src/agents/session-types.ts:235, while DispatchErrorEvent currently lacks them at src/runtime/dispatch-events.ts:130. Error aggregates must include error cost separately in every snapshot path (overall, grouped, scoped) without changing successful totalCostUsd; drain already serializes the error union. The manager file has a size-baseline constraint, so replace individual identifiers with the existing options object as specified rather than adding lines.

US-002 changes pruneRetainedTranscripts in src/agents/native/session/transcript-store.ts:165 from a void operation to a deletion count; it currently recognizes live and failed transcript names and is only invoked from a close path. The new sweep must use deriveNativeTranscriptDir from src/session/manager-deps.ts:45 rather than reconstructing paths, export through both barrel layers (src/agents/native/index.ts and src/session/index.ts), and be invoked during startup next to sessionManager.sweepOrphans() in src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:381. src/session/scratch-purge.ts provides the injectable, feature-scoped utility shape, but has no production-call implication. Existing transcript-store tests currently assert the old undefined return for a missing directory (test/unit/agents/native/transcript-store.test.ts:115), so update those expectations as part of the widening migration.

US-003 replaces the direct buildCodingToolSupport call in src/session/manager-run.ts:70. resolveCodingToolSupport in src/agents/coding-tool-support.ts:103 resolves permissions, audit directory, ledger session name, and preserves the existing CODING_TOOL_ROOT_MISSING failure. Only apply resolved support when the caller did not supply codingToolRuntime, avoiding an overwrite; no dispatch event should be added because the runner remains the turn-event producer. The SessionManager.runInSession runner-shaped path is the production seam and existing tests include test/unit/session/manager-run-in-session.test.ts.

US-004 adds an injected identity claim to _planDeps in src/cli/plan-runtime.ts and runs it before buildPlanModeContext in src/cli/plan-command.ts:79. Mirror the identity derivation/remote lookup/collision handling at src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:339-359; claimProjectIdentity itself throws RUN_NAME_COLLISION for foreign workdirs in src/runtime/paths.ts:75. A collision must abort before strategy creation/dispatch; other claim errors warn and allow planning. Existing plan tests are concentrated under test/unit/cli/plan*.test.ts and run under isolated global config.

Compatibility and migration: all public event and row additions are optional, except the intentional private builder-input reshape and prune return widening. Existing DispatchErrorEvent literals remain valid; preserve undefined tokens for usage-less failures, rather than emitting zero-token data. Ledger readers must tolerate older JSONL rows without the new fields/schema changes; no data backfill is required. The four stories are independent, and only US-002 creates src/session/transcript-sweep.ts.
outOfScope: Recording spend for a session killed by `SIGKILL`, which no handler can catch; addressing it would require flushing cost per round trip rather than per op.
Including failed-dispatch spend in `CostSnapshot.totalCostUsd`; failed spend is reported separately as `totalErrorCostUsd`.
Adding model attribution (`model`, `pricingSource`) to `DispatchErrorEvent`; only `sessionRole` and usage are added.
Closing warm-lifetime native sessions at run end; retention is made independent of the close path instead.
Changing `MAX_RETAINED_TRANSCRIPTS` from 50, or making it configurable.
Wiring a production caller for `SessionRunClient`; `runTrackedSession` stays reachable only from `SessionManager.runInSession`.
Wiring `purgeStaleScratch`, which has no production caller today.
Any change to `nax migrate --reclaim` / `--merge`, or to collision recovery generally.
Extending the collision guard to `nax resume`, `nax replay`, or any command other than `nax plan`.
US-001 only: reporting failed spend in the `nax cost` CLI output.
